$comment: Read from Google's Drive v3 discovery document: files.create -> POST files, request File, response File. The discovery document's servicePath is drive/v3/, so the full metadata-only path is /drive/v3/files -- not /files and not a guessed /v3/files.
title: Google Drive folder
description: Create a folder in Google Drive.
$idempotencyComment: files.create declares no idempotency key. Retrying can create a SECOND folder with the same name, because Drive names are not unique within a folder.

constants.$comment: This is a metadata-only create. The folder MIME type is Google's declared type for a Drive folder; no upload URI or media body is involved.

config.label: Folder name
config.description: The folder name. Drive does not require names to be unique within a parent.

config.label: Parent folder IDs
config.description: Parent folder ids, comma separated. Leave empty to create the folder in My Drive.
config.$comment: File.parents is an array of STRINGS. A file can have only one parent even though the schema remains an array; multiple parents are no longer supported. encoding array is the exact existing vocabulary -- this is neither rows nor objects.

outputShape.description: The fixed Google Drive folder MIME type.
The parent folder id array returned by Drive.

$outputComment: files.create returns the File directly at the response top level; the connector runtime exposes that body under data, with no {file: ...} wrapper.

contract.$comment: The File fields this action sends and reads, used by discovery drift projection.
